semantics.status: unnumbered dev, no legacy filed compatibility
semantics.transport: kb2_vq readable request and writable response descriptor chains; capacities are negotiated, not filesystem limits
semantics.spans: offsets from the start of the complete readable request; zero length requires zero offset; nonempty spans start after the header and may not overlap; groups are aligned little-endian u32
semantics.paths: NUL-terminated Linux paths including the terminator; no embedded NUL; Linux owns PATH_MAX and NAME_MAX validation
semantics.credentials: owner-only CLIENT_REGISTER/CREDENTIALS carry the complete credentials record in data, aligned supplementary groups and filesystem capability rights in request.capabilities; the service retains rights and Linux cred together, never derives authority from data-request capabilities, uid, gid or groups; ordinary dispatch selects the client from an authenticated queue binding; optional nonzero client and credential_generation claims must match that binding and its current credentials; zero claims select the binding and current credentials, not the owner; request uid/gid are chown operands, not identity
semantics.authorization: filesystem capability rights supplement Linux DAC, never replace it; operation authorization and VFS execution consume the same immutable request snapshot and the same retained rights/cred pair; data dispatch rejects management/frontend operations even for a client with all rights; owner updates atomically publish the new rights/cred pair; already admitted operations may retain the previous pair, whereas admission after the update ACK uses the new pair
semantics.exec_payload: data contains exec_payload header with relative spans; argv/envp span tables contain exec_string records with NUL-terminated strings relative to the same payload; grants, handles and patches use exec_grant, u64, exec_patch respectively; counts must exactly match span lengths; flags equal request flags; no fixed argv/envp/string caps beyond native launch resource limits
semantics.handles: opaque monotonically minted file references scoped to sandbox generation and authenticated client; zero selects that client's granted root for directory operations
semantics.results: negative Linux errno or nonnegative syscall result; file references use the separate handle field; raw linux_dirent64 and Linux statx/statfs records are explicitly serialized little-endian payloads
semantics.response: data immediately follows the response header; used length is exactly header plus data_length; errors have no data or handle; echoed opcode, generation and sequence must match the owned request
semantics.flags: Linux syscall flags are passed without a filed-specific translation; umask applies only to creation, and syncfs is scoped to the granted filesystem
semantics.ownership: descriptor payloads are leased until completion; the service snapshots all untrusted inputs before entering Linux; no host FD or native pointer crosses this format
semantics.snapshot: STATX mode=1 (snapshot_query) requests snapshot_stat, only for a readable regular-file handle with AT_EMPTY_PATH and no pathname; snapshot_metadata flags bit 0 asserts an actual Linux change cookie and the inode generation (including legitimate zero) with no writable open descriptions or shared writable mappings; otherwise flags is zero, never a guessed timestamp cookie. PREAD mode=1 requests a cookie sampled after that read in response.handle and snapshot validity flags in response.service; flags zero means invalid. Result and data_length remain the read byte count, preserving direct copies into the destination VMO. Consumers compare against the initial stat and never cache a mismatched or invalid copy. FILE_VMO response.handle is the page-aligned offset into the transferred VMO, result remains the requested range bytes read. For STATX and PREAD only, mode is a protocol selector: 0 preserves the ordinary Linux operation, 1 requests snapshot validation, and other values are rejected. It is independent of Linux mask/flags; application statx mask 0x40000000 (kernel-only STATX_CHANGE_COOKIE) is ignored and never selects snapshot_stat. No version negotiation or compatibility alias.
semantics.shared_file_vmo: owner-only authenticated export of real Linux regular-file/shmem page-cache pages; offset and length are page-aligned and length is nonzero; flags bits 0 and 1 request future WRITE and EXEC ceilings, mask holds initial Linux PROT bits 0..2; READ filesystem capability is mandatory with WRITE/EXEC capabilities for the respective ceilings; Linux file mode, seals, noexec and mmap security may further attenuate rights; response handle is an opaque export ID and result is file size; native VMO capability is transferred separately on the authenticated management channel, bound to generation, client, sequence and export ID, never encoded as a wire FD; pages beyond EOF are sparse unavailable backing, not zero-filled anonymous pages; refresh retires native translations before Linux releases old folio pins; reclamation requires confirmed native capability/mapping exclusivity and revocation
semantics.session_config: authenticated frontend HELLO flags=1 reserves a fresh queue binding for that client; length selects a minimum arena budget, zero selects the configured default; response data is queue_config and handle is the fresh channel_id, never the client ID; SESSION_ATTACH uses that exact generation, channel_id, arena size and queue depth with one RW VMO and one dedicated notification endpoint; frontend forwards capabilities on the owner-only management channel and replies only after sandbox installation ACK; no request payload is relayed
semantics.session_detach: authenticated frontend control operation; exactly one request header with no capability transfers; generation selects the reserved session generation and second_handle its fresh channel_id; all other operation operands and spans are zero; request client and credential metadata cannot confer authority; success echoes channel_id in response.handle only after sandbox quiesces the queue, unmaps it and closes its retained capabilities; managed client identity and file references remain alive; uncertain retirement is not acknowledged and retains the unresolved inventory
semantics.device_route: frontend-only operation with OPENAT2 directory/path/flags operands and the same filesystem capability requirements; only a side-effect-free O_PATH lookup and device/service classification are allowed, never the original open or a general filesystem retry; ordinary clients use it only after direct OPENAT2 returns ENXIO/ENODEV; success returns the retained O_PATH handle, host service tag and encoded statx for that exact pinned device, so the client opens the selected native service without resolving the pathname again; non-device or unroutable paths fail without ordinary open, creation, truncation or data I/O
